info.name: OpenRegister API: configuration, user settings, organisations, tags, views, templates, chat, conversations, file text
info.description:
Covers the API routes of ConfigurationController, UserSettingsController, SearchController, OrganisationController, OrganisationHaltController, TagsController, ViewsController, RecordTemplatesController, ChatController, ConversationController and FileTextController: for each route the success path, an unknown id, invalid input where the method validates, and the answer to a non-admin user without rights next to the admin or owner who may.

SELF-CONTAINED: the `00 setup` folder seeds its own register, schema, two objects and two non-admin users (via the OCS provisioning API) and stores their ids in collection variables; every folder creates and removes what else it needs, and `99 teardown` deletes the seed data. Nothing depends on another collection's data or on run order.

Routes that need a service CI does not have (GitHub/GitLab, a remote URL, an LLM) are asserted on their documented answer when that service is absent or unconfigured.

Variables: base_url (default http://localhost:8080), admin_user, admin_password.

exec: // Nextcloud answers a basic-auth request with a session cookie; newman's jar would replay it on the
// next request and authenticate it as the previous caller. Clear it so each request is only its own auth.

item.name: 30d record templates
item.description: RecordTemplatesController: index/show are NoAdminRequired+NoCSRFRequired; create/update/patch/destroy are NoAdminRequired but CSRF-checked, so an API client must send OCS-APIRequest: true (basic auth alone answers 412). An admin-owned private template drives the access tests: user A has no reach and must get 404.

exec: pm.test('CSRF refusal, no template in body', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/CSRF/i); pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('uuid'); });
